verdict.rationale: MoonPay documents a headless, API-driven path. You can build your own on-ramp and off-ramp on its APIs and SDKs, submit KYC via the Customer API, call the Platform API server-side, and generate clients from an OpenAPI 3.1 spec. However, key steps still depend on MoonPay-hosted UI: card capture runs in a PCI-compliant MoonPay frame, verification uses a self-driving challenge frame, and authentication uses an Auth frame. That is not pure API parity with the UI. Missing for 10: API-only equivalents for card entry, verification challenges and auth/MFA; documented API coverage of swaps and off-ramp steps; independent confirmation of full parity (the OpenAPI spec was not found at the probed public paths).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Build your own on-ramp and off-ramp on MoonPay's APIs and SDKs. Your UI, your flow, our rails.
The API-driven path: capture KYC data in your own screens and submit it with the Customer API.
forward the accessToken to your own backend and call the MoonPay Platform API server-side on that customer's behalf.
The MoonPay Developer Platform API is defined using an OpenAPI 3.1 specification.
Card data is captured inside a PCI-compliant MoonPay-hosted UI and never touches your domain.
